_README: Open-Meteo dataset for the requested location. Run: python scripts/fetch_openmeteo.py  (needs internet). Keys starting with '_' are comments. Values marked PLACEHOLDER are reasonable starting points that YOU should confirm for the real farm.
name: openmeteo_11.93975_79.49244
_PLACEHOLDER_period: PLACEHOLDER(openmeteo): download period. The archive lags ~5 days behind today; archived forecasts (for the rain-forecast parameter) exist from about 2022 onwards. 4 years = ~35,000 hourly rows.
_PLACEHOLDER_soil_layers: PLACEHOLDER(openmeteo): archive soil-moisture layers averaged by thickness (cm) to mimic a probe at ~0-28 cm. Add "soil_moisture_28_to_100cm": 72 for a deeper root zone.
_PLACEHOLDER_soil_type: PLACEHOLDER(openmeteo): 'auto' picks the soil class whose field capacity / wilting point best match the downloaded moisture (field capacity = moisture 48 h after >= 10 mm rain). Replace with the farm's measured texture (sandy | sandy_loam | loam | clay_loam | clay) when known.
_PLACEHOLDER_irrigation_method: PLACEHOLDER(openmeteo): drip | sprinkler | furrow on the real farm.
_PLACEHOLDER_seasons: PLACEHOLDER(openmeteo): the farm's crop calendar. Each entry repeats every year; every season becomes one 'field' in the dataset. Example values only - replace with the actual crops and sowing dates. Crops: cotton | groundnut | maize | onion | potato | tomato | wheat (paddy rice is out of scope).
_rain_forecast: Use archived Open-Meteo forecasts as the 24 h rain forecast (true forecasts). If false or unavailable, observed next-24h rain is used as a perfect-forecast proxy (flagged in column forecast_source).
